gallery.credit: Dunkin, Edwin Hadlow Wise, The Monumental Brasses of Cornwall with Descriptive, Geneaological and Heraldic Notes, 1882, Plate XXX, pp. 34-5
gallery.source: SirJohnIVArundell OfTrerice Died1561 StrattonChurch Cornwall Detail
gallery.description: Monumental brass in Stratton Church, Cornwall, of Sir John IV Arundell (1495–1561), known as "Jack of Tilbury", an Esquire of the Body to King Henry VIII whom he served as Vice-Admiral of the West. He was knighted at the Battle of the Spurs in 1513. In 1523 he achieved notability by the capture of a notorious pirate. He served twice as Sheriff of Cornwall, in 1532 and in 1541

gallery.title: File:Huers house.jpg
gallery.description:
The huer's house at Newquay where the "huer" would watch out for pilchard shoals and let the fisherman know when they were around. It is a Grade II* listed building.


This is a photo of listed building number 1144136.
